faq.a: Enayat is associated with the Arabic form عِنَايَت, whose core sense is enayat; care, providence.

faq.q: What is the origin of Enayat?
faq.a: Enayat is associated with Arabic. Enayat is Arabic عِنَايَة (ʿInāya), meaning 'care, providence'. It is used as a given name in South Asia and Iran.
Yes — the underlying form عِنَايَت is Arabic.
Enayat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Enayat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿInāya is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Enayat mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Enayat is rendered عنایت and carries the sense عنایت، مہربانی.

faq.q: What does Enayat mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Enayat is rendered عنایت and carries the sense عنایت، لطف.
A romanized syllable approximation is e-nayat. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Enayat?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Enayat, enayat. Script forms are عنايت, عنایت, عِنَايَت, इनायत.

faq.q: Is Enayat a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
